judge_assessment.explanation: Every solution the judge lists is right and I solved each system independently: (10,30) tickets; (11,7) metres; (15,3) km/h; (2,3) dollars; (2,5) dollars; (90,110) tickets; (10,70) months and dollars; (6,2) kilograms; no solution on the two receipts (doubling 2x+3y=19 gives 4x+6y=38, not 34); and (7,5) for the equipment, with the catalogue claim failing because 6(7)+4(5)=62, not 60. Units and named variables are indeed explicit in every stem, as the judge says. Two things the judge did not check. First, problem 9's 'no solution' is a genuinely verified result - gate_log.txt line 30 reads '[PASS] Problem 9: system[...] -> inconsistent: no solution, as the key states' - but the Quick Answers bank prints '9. -'. verify.json encodes it as expected [], render_entry joins zero values into an empty string, and the fallback prints the em-dash that the module documents as meaning manual-only. So the sheet's one special case has no answer on the grading page even though the verifier confirmed it. Second, four stems print an explanation slot with no manual entry: problem 4 ('Explain in one line which operation - adding or subtracting - removes x'), problem 5 ('Say which equation you scale and by what'), problem 8 ('Choose a variable, write the two multipliers you will use'), and above all problem 9 ('Write down exactly what happens, say what the result tells you about the two receipts, and explain what it means for these two lines that they never meet'). The only manual entry in the file is the second entry on id 10, for part (b). Problem 9 is the item where the method choice IS the answer, and it is recorded as fully machine-verified.

strengths_to_preserve: Every stem names the variables with their units before the system appears - 'Let x be the boat's speed in still water and y the current's speed, both in km/h', 'Let x be the length in metres and y the width in metres' - and then prints the system beneath the story. The translation step is removed on purpose so the algebra is the task, which is exactly what the prompt's 'state units and givens explicitly' asks for.

The method is chosen by the problem rather than announced by the section heading: problem 3 says 'The y terms are already opposites. Add the equations'; problem 4 says 'Nothing needs multiplying here'; problem 5 says 'Multiplying one equation is enough'; problem 8 says 'no coefficient matches, so both equations must be scaled'. The three facets are interleaved (substitution on 1, 2, 7; add/subtract on 3, 4; scaling on 5, 6, 8, 9, 10) instead of blocked.

Problem 9's context does real work: two receipts from the same shop on the same day that cannot both be right turns 'no solution' from an algebraic curiosity into a claim about the world, and the key ties the collapse to parallel lines.

Problem 10 is a genuine challenge rather than a longer problem: part (a) is solved and checked in both original purchases, and part (b) introduces a third equation that contradicts the first two, with a properly declared manual entry whose desc states what the reviewer should look for ('No single value to compute - read the student's reasoning').

root_causes.description: A verified empty solution set is rendered as the manual glyph. verify.py treats expected [] as a first-class assertion of inconsistency and PASSes it, but render_entry returns '---' whenever the joined expected text is empty, so the checked answer 'no solution' and an unchecked open response are printed identically.
evidence: verify.json id 9 expected []; gate_log.txt line 30 records PASS with 'inconsistent: no solution, as the key states'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry: 'return text if text else "---"' - an empty expected list produces empty text.
answer_key.pdf page 1 Quick Answers row '9. -'; the worked solution states the collapse to 0 = 4 and the no-solution conclusion in full.
The same document's row 10 prints 'x = 7, y = 5' even though id 10 also carries a manual entry, so the em-dash on row 9 is the only blank on the page and reads as an omission.

root_causes.description: Method-choice and interpretation slots are treated as covered by the numeric solution they accompany. The sheet asks the student to state which operation eliminates, which equation to scale and by what, and what the collapse of problem 9 means; only the fully open part (b) of problem 10 is declared manual, so four reasoning slots are recorded as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 9: 'Write down exactly what happens, say what the result tells you about the two receipts, and explain what it means for these two lines that they never meet.' verify.json id 9 holds one system entry and no manual entry.

improvements.title: Print 'no solution' for problem 9 instead of the glyph reserved for manual items
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers.render_entry, render an entry whose expected is an empty list as the words 'no solution' rather than letting the empty join fall through to '---', and reserve '---' for ids whose entries are all type manual. Take the wording from one shared constant so the bank and the key cannot disagree.
improvements.regression_test: Render this task's verify.json and assert the id 9 row reads 'no solution' while a manual-only id still renders '---'. Today row 9 prints '-', so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after; curr-227's id 8 gives the same fixture for the graphing case.
improvements.expected_impact: The one special case on the sheet regains a printed answer on the grading page, and the em-dash stops carrying two meanings inside a document that has a real manual item on problem 10.
improvements.risk: Very low - a local change in one function, with the wording centralised.

improvements.title: Declare manual entries for problem 9's interpretation and the method-choice slots in 4, 5 and 8
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response verb scan to the gate chain so stems containing 'explain', 'say what', 'say which' or 'write down exactly what happens' force a manual entry on that id. Here ids 4, 5, 8 and 9 gain manual entries alongside their system checks; problem 9's should carry the reviewer criterion the key already states (the student must connect 0 = 4 to parallel lines and to the two receipts being inconsistent).
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 9's stem and a verify.json id 9 holding only the system entry with expected []. The check must exit non-zero naming the interpretation slot; adding a manual entry makes it pass while leaving the system entry's PASS intact.
improvements.expected_impact: On the one problem where the algebra produces no number, the student's explanation - the only thing there is to grade - reaches a reviewer instead of being covered by an empty solution set.
improvements.risk: Four more manual items on a ten-problem sheet; the matcher must be scoped to the problem body so the 'Before you solve, decide how' directions block does not trigger on every id.

case_summary: Ten applied systems, all solved correctly by the methods the stems request, with variables and units named in every context, the three solution methods interleaved rather than blocked, and a challenge problem whose part (b) introduces a contradictory third equation and is properly declared manual. Two defects remain. Problem 9's 'no solution' is verified and PASSing, yet the Quick Answers bank prints '9. -' because render_entry maps an empty expected list onto the manual glyph, so the sheet's one special case has no answer on the grading page. And four stems - problems 4, 5, 8 and above all 9, where the collapse to 0 = 4 and what it says about the two receipts is the entire answer - print explanation slots with no manual entry, leaving problem 10(b) as the file's only declared reviewable item.
